lessons.title: Metrics
lessons.summary: Aggregated measurements of system behavior over time.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Metric dimensions affect both usefulness and storage cost.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A team needs to track request rate and error ratio over time. Instrument suitable counters and derive rates with clear dimensions.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every metric is a complete individual request record. This is not a sound assumption; aggregated measurements of system behavior over time.

lessons.takeaway: Metric dimensions affect both usefulness and storage cost.

lessons.title: Logs
lessons.summary: Discrete event records with contextual detail.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Structured fields make filtering and correlation more reliable.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Incident diagnosis requires finding failures for one operation. Use structured operation identifiers and relevant error fields.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Logs always provide an unbiased statistical sample. This is not a sound assumption; discrete event records with contextual detail.

lessons.takeaway: Structured fields make filtering and correlation more reliable.

lessons.title: Traces
lessons.summary: Related spans representing work across a request path.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Trace propagation is needed to connect work across boundaries.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A request crosses services but appears as disconnected traces. Verify context propagation across the relevant boundaries.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every trace contains all requests ever processed. This is not a sound assumption; related spans representing work across a request path.

lessons.takeaway: Trace propagation is needed to connect work across boundaries.

lessons.title: Counters
lessons.summary: It accumulates events and may reset when its producer restarts.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rate calculations must account for resets.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service restart makes the raw request counter fall. Use an appropriate reset-aware rate calculation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A counter is intended to fluctuate freely with current temperature. This is not a sound assumption; it accumulates events and may reset when its producer restarts.

lessons.takeaway: Rate calculations must account for resets.

lessons.title: Gauges
lessons.summary: A value that can rise or fall such as queue depth.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: A gauge snapshot does not automatically describe all events between samples.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A queue briefly spikes between scrape intervals. Review sampling and complementary event or age measurements.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Gauges must only increase forever. This is not a sound assumption; a value that can rise or fall such as queue depth.

lessons.takeaway: A gauge snapshot does not automatically describe all events between samples.

lessons.title: Histograms
lessons.summary: A distribution of observations using buckets or supported histogram structures.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Bucket design affects useful resolution around important thresholds.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A latency SLO threshold lies inside a very wide bucket. Choose resolution around the operational threshold.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A histogram is only a single average. This is not a sound assumption; a distribution of observations using buckets or supported histogram structures.

lessons.takeaway: Bucket design affects useful resolution around important thresholds.

lessons.title: Labels
lessons.summary: Each unique label combination can create another time series.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Unbounded identifiers can create major cost and reliability problems.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A metric adds a request ID label and series count explodes. Remove unbounded labels and use logs or traces for per-request identity.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: User IDs are always safe low-cardinality metric labels. This is not a sound assumption; each unique label combination can create another time series.

lessons.takeaway: Unbounded identifiers can create major cost and reliability problems.

lessons.title: Dashboards
lessons.summary: It supports specific questions about service behavior and impact.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Clear units windows and aggregation prevent misinterpretation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Responders cannot tell whether a graph shows totals or rates. Label units and queries and organize around operational questions.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: More panels always mean better incident response. This is not a sound assumption; it supports specific questions about service behavior and impact.

lessons.takeaway: Clear units windows and aggregation prevent misinterpretation.

lessons.title: Rate before aggregation
lessons.summary: Per-series reset detection can be lost after combining counters.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Counter identity matters when instances restart independently.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: One instance restarts and an aggregate traffic graph spikes incorrectly. Compute reset-aware rates per counter series before aggregation.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Summing raw counters always preserves every reset correctly. This is not a sound assumption; per-series reset detection can be lost after combining counters.

lessons.takeaway: Counter identity matters when instances restart independently.

lessons.title: Percentiles
lessons.summary: An average of quantiles is not the quantile of the combined distribution.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Aggregate compatible distributions before estimating fleet quantiles.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Two instances have very different traffic and latency distributions. Aggregate suitable histogram data for the desired population.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: The average of p99 values is always the fleet p99. This is not a sound assumption; an average of quantiles is not the quantile of the combined distribution.

lessons.takeaway: Aggregate compatible distributions before estimating fleet quantiles.

lessons.title: Missing data
lessons.summary: Absence can mean collection or service failure rather than zero activity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Missing-data policy should match the alert's intended meaning.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An error-rate alert goes quiet when scraping stops. Monitor collection health and define explicit missing-data behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: No samples always prove no errors occurred. This is not a sound assumption; absence can mean collection or service failure rather than zero activity.

lessons.takeaway: Missing-data policy should match the alert's intended meaning.

lessons.title: Scrape health
lessons.summary: The collector could not obtain the expected metrics response.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: The cause may be target failure or a collection-path problem.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A target scrape fails while user traffic still succeeds. Inspect scrape errors and distinguish telemetry reachability from service behavior.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: It always proves all user requests failed. This is not a sound assumption; the collector could not obtain the expected metrics response.

lessons.takeaway: The cause may be target failure or a collection-path problem.

lessons.title: Recording rules
lessons.summary: Precompute useful derived time series for repeated queries.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rule correctness and evaluation cost still need review.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A frequently used expensive dashboard query overloads the backend. Evaluate a suitable precomputed rule and validate its semantics.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Recording rules automatically make incorrect queries correct. This is not a sound assumption; precompute useful derived time series for repeated queries.

lessons.takeaway: Rule correctness and evaluation cost still need review.

lessons.title: Alert duration
lessons.summary: Pages caused by brief threshold crossings.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Long delays can also postpone detection of genuine incidents.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An alert pages repeatedly on harmless short spikes. Tune duration with impact and detection-time requirements.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Any delay always improves every alert. This is not a sound assumption; pages caused by brief threshold crossings.

lessons.takeaway: Long delays can also postpone detection of genuine incidents.

lessons.title: Alert grouping
lessons.summary: Reduce duplicated notifications about the same operational event.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Grouping must preserve enough context to identify affected services.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: One dependency outage causes dozens of similar pages. Group correlated notifications and identify the likely shared incident.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Grouping means discarding all but one underlying signal forever. This is not a sound assumption; reduce duplicated notifications about the same operational event.

lessons.takeaway: Grouping must preserve enough context to identify affected services.

lessons.title: Alert inhibition
lessons.summary: Suppress lower-level notifications when a related higher-level condition applies.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Rules must avoid hiding unrelated genuine incidents.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A host-down event triggers many derivative service alerts. Use carefully scoped inhibition while retaining evidence.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Inhibition deletes the underlying metric data. This is not a sound assumption; suppress lower-level notifications when a related higher-level condition applies.

lessons.takeaway: Rules must avoid hiding unrelated genuine incidents.

lessons.title: Sampling
lessons.summary: Reduce volume at the cost of retaining only part of traffic.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Sampling policy affects which questions retained traces can answer.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Rare failures are absent from a low-rate head-sampled dataset. Review sampling policy and error-retention requirements.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Sampled traces are automatically a complete record of every error. This is not a sound assumption; reduce volume at the cost of retaining only part of traffic.

lessons.takeaway: Sampling policy affects which questions retained traces can answer.

lessons.title: Tail sampling
lessons.summary: Decisions can use information collected about a trace after processing.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Buffering completeness and decision latency introduce operational costs.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A team wants to retain slow and failed traces preferentially. Evaluate tail sampling with capacity and completeness constraints.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Tail sampling requires no memory or coordination. This is not a sound assumption; decisions can use information collected about a trace after processing.

lessons.takeaway: Buffering completeness and decision latency introduce operational costs.

lessons.title: Context propagation
lessons.summary: Context may not be carried through queues or task boundaries automatically.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Message metadata and instrumentation need deliberate propagation.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A queued worker starts unrelated traces for each job. Propagate the appropriate trace context through supported message metadata.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Thread-local context automatically crosses every process and queue. This is not a sound assumption; context may not be carried through queues or task boundaries automatically.

lessons.takeaway: Message metadata and instrumentation need deliberate propagation.

lessons.title: Correlation
lessons.summary: Shared identifiers connect detailed events to request paths.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Correlation requires consistent identifiers and suitable access controls.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: An error log is difficult to connect to a slow request. Include relevant trace or operation identifiers in structured logs.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: A timestamp alone always uniquely identifies a distributed request. This is not a sound assumption; shared identifiers connect detailed events to request paths.

lessons.takeaway: Correlation requires consistent identifiers and suitable access controls.

lessons.title: Sensitive telemetry
lessons.summary: Logs traces and labels can become secondary stores of private data.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Collection controls retention and access policy all matter.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Request headers containing credentials are exported in traces. Stop or redact collection and address existing exposure.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Observability data is automatically exempt from privacy requirements. This is not a sound assumption; logs traces and labels can become secondary stores of private data.

lessons.takeaway: Collection controls retention and access policy all matter.

lessons.title: Retention
lessons.summary: Balance operational investigation requirements cost and data sensitivity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Different signal types may justify different retention periods.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Incident analysis needs data already removed by an overly short policy. Review investigation windows and set deliberate tiered retention.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: All telemetry should be kept forever regardless of sensitivity. This is not a sound assumption; balance operational investigation requirements cost and data sensitivity.

lessons.takeaway: Different signal types may justify different retention periods.

lessons.title: Telemetry pipelines
lessons.summary: Delivery delay or loss when telemetry production exceeds processing capacity.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Buffers retries and drop behavior need explicit monitoring.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Telemetry disappears during peak load while applications still run. Inspect collector queues drops and downstream capacity.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Collectors have infinite buffering by default. This is not a sound assumption; delivery delay or loss when telemetry production exceeds processing capacity.

lessons.takeaway: Buffers retries and drop behavior need explicit monitoring.

lessons.title: Resource identity
lessons.summary: Identify the service environment and instance producing telemetry.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Inconsistent identity makes cross-signal queries unreliable.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Production and staging telemetry appear under indistinguishable identities. Standardize service and environment attributes.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Every exporter automatically knows the correct deployment environment. This is not a sound assumption; identify the service environment and instance producing telemetry.

lessons.takeaway: Inconsistent identity makes cross-signal queries unreliable.

lessons.title: Clock skew
lessons.summary: Timestamps across hosts may imply a misleading event order.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Trace relationships and measured durations provide context beyond wall time.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A downstream log appears earlier than the upstream request. Inspect time synchronization and causal identifiers.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Wall timestamps always establish exact causal order. This is not a sound assumption; timestamps across hosts may imply a misleading event order.

lessons.takeaway: Trace relationships and measured durations provide context beyond wall time.

lessons.title: RED signals
lessons.summary: Rate errors and duration.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Resource saturation signals can complement request-centric indicators.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A service needs an initial user-impact dashboard. Measure traffic error behavior and latency with clear request definitions.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: RED means only disk capacity and host uptime. This is not a sound assumption; rate errors and duration.

lessons.takeaway: Resource saturation signals can complement request-centric indicators.

lessons.title: USE signals
lessons.summary: Utilization saturation and errors.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Resource analysis complements service-level symptoms.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A device shows moderate utilization but growing queues. Inspect saturation and errors as well as utilization.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: USE is a substitute for every user-facing SLI. This is not a sound assumption; utilization saturation and errors.

lessons.takeaway: Resource analysis complements service-level symptoms.

lessons.title: Synthetic checks
lessons.summary: Active checks of selected user journeys or endpoints.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Synthetic coverage is limited to what the check actually exercises.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: A homepage check passes while checkout is broken. Add a representative checkout check with safe test data.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: One successful synthetic proves every user path works. This is not a sound assumption; active checks of selected user journeys or endpoints.

lessons.takeaway: Synthetic coverage is limited to what the check actually exercises.

lessons.title: Instrumentation cost
lessons.summary: Telemetry collection can consume CPU memory network and storage.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Sampling batching and cardinality controls can reduce cost.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Detailed tracing adds material latency under peak load. Measure overhead and tune collection to preserve useful evidence.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Instrumentation has zero performance impact by definition. This is not a sound assumption; telemetry collection can consume CPU memory network and storage.

lessons.takeaway: Sampling batching and cardinality controls can reduce cost.

lessons.title: Evidence and causality
lessons.summary: Simultaneous changes do not prove one caused the other.

sections.heading: How it works
sections.body: Hypotheses need supporting evidence and controlled verification where possible.

sections.heading: Apply it
sections.body: Latency and CPU rise together after a release. Test a plausible causal hypothesis using traces changes and dependency evidence.

sections.heading: Misconception to challenge
sections.body: Two aligned graph spikes prove a causal relationship. This is not a sound assumption; simultaneous changes do not prove one caused the other.

lessons.takeaway: Hypotheses need supporting evidence and controlled verification where possible.
